issues.legal_issue: A court may refuse permission to make up a deficit in court fee when an appellant deliberately paid a fee for a restricted claim and sought to increase the claim only after the appeal had been heard.
material_facts: In appeals concerning compensation for acquired land, the claimants valued their appeals at lower amounts and paid court fees calculated on those amounts, although they sought higher compensation.
Some applications to pay the deficit court fee were made after arguments had been heard and judgment was reserved; other applications were made after judgment was pronounced.
The court found no bona fide reason for the claimants’ failure to pay the requisite fee earlier and considered that they had waited to gauge the likely outcome.
issues.conclusion: The court was not required to permit payment of the deficit court fee and properly refused permission. The claimants’ appeals were dismissed, the Union’s appeals were allowed, and adjudication of the claimants’ appeals was confined to the amounts on which court fee had been paid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 149 of the Code of Civil Procedure confers judicial discretion, not an entitlement, to allow a party to make up a court-fee deficiency. Ordinarily, sufficient cause or a bona fide mistake is required; mere poverty, ignorance, or inability to pay is not invariably sufficient. A deliberate choice to pay less, followed by a request to increase the claim after the appeal has been heard, is not a bona fide mistake and may be refused. The court also referred to Section 148 and Order 41 Rule 9 CPC, the applicable Court Fee Act provisions, and Scheduled Caste Co-operative Land Owning Society Ltd. v. Union of India, whose ratio the Constitution Bench had approved; it noted that Chand Kuar v. Union of India had been decided without noticing that authority.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and restricted_fee_paid and deliberate_underpayment and post_hearing_fee_request and no_bona_fide_reason

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is an appeal in which the appellant seeks a determination of a claim.
predicates.restricted_fee_paid: The appellant paid court fee calculated on a claim valued below the higher claim later pursued.
predicates.deliberate_underpayment: The appellant chose to pay less court fee rather than pay the fee required for the higher claim when presenting the appeal.
predicates.post_hearing_fee_request: The appellant asked to make up the fee deficiency after the appeal had been heard or its likely outcome had become apparent.
predicates.no_bona_fide_reason: The appellant had no bona fide mistake or other sufficient reason for failing to pay the required fee earlier.

issues.definition: When an appellant deliberately pays fee on a restricted claim and, without a bona fide reason, seeks to pay more only after the appeal has been heard, the court may deny permission to make up the deficiency.

issues.legal_issue: The fact that an appeal remains pending does not, by itself, entitle an appellant who restricted the appeal’s valuation to pay deficit court fee after enhanced compensation has been determined.
material_facts: The claimants relied on an earlier decision concerning appeals that had remained pending, arguing that this allowed them to pay deficit court fee for higher compensation.
The earlier decision involved claimants who had restricted their claim and paid court fee on that valuation, then sought to pay more after compensation was further enhanced.
The court stated that the Constitution Bench had approved the ratio of that earlier decision and that its observations had to be understood in the context of its facts.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision did not establish a general right to pay deficit court fee after an appeal had been allowed and higher compensation determined. The claimants were not entitled to rely on the pendency of their appeals to increase claims for which they had deliberately paid a lower court fee.
issues.legal_principle: Scheduled Caste Co-operative Land Owning Society Ltd. v. Union of India, as approved by the Constitution Bench, does not mean that an appellant who chose a lower valuation may pay deficit court fee after the appeal has been allowed and higher compensation fixed. Its observations must be read in their factual context; a pending appeal alone does not displace the requirement to value the appeal and pay the corresponding fee. The court distinguished the contrary approach in Chand Kuar v. Union of India, which had not noticed the earlier decision.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and appeal_remains_pending and restricted_fee_paid and higher_claim_sought_after_determination

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is an appeal in which the appellant seeks a determination of a claim.
predicates.appeal_remains_pending: The appeal has not yet concluded when the appellant seeks to change the claim.
predicates.restricted_fee_paid: The appellant paid court fee calculated on a claim valued below the higher claim later pursued.
predicates.higher_claim_sought_after_determination: The appellant seeks to pay more court fee for a higher claim after the amount recoverable has been determined.

issues.definition: An appellant who paid fee on a restricted claim cannot rely only on the appeal remaining pending to seek a higher claim after its value has been determined.
